requirements.requirement: Prevent the usb-storage kernel module from loading on node1 in the current boot.
requirements.summary: The module was initially unloaded. After the deny policy was installed, an explicit modprobe attempt failed with the install rule `/bin/false`, and usb_storage remained unloaded.

requirements.requirement: Ensure usb-storage remains blocked after node1 reboots.
requirements.summary: A bounded reboot was observed: node1 began healthy, acknowledged the scheduled reboot, changed boot ID, and recovered to a running state with a read-write root filesystem. Afterward, the persistent policy remained present, an explicit load attempt failed, usb_storage was not loaded, and the rebuilt initramfs omitted the module. Fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot-ID change.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-reboot behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is coherent for the single managed node and is independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities. Minor hygiene deductions apply for a superseded initramfs rebuild and two retained scratch files.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required configuration, final initramfs rebuild, verification, and reboot were appropriately scoped. One unnecessary mutation occurred: the first initramfs rebuild did not embed the policy or omit the module and was superseded by the later successful rebuild, so it was effectively reverted/overwritten. Two evidence probes also left `/tmp/usb-storage-load.out` and `/tmp/usb-storage-postboot.out` behind rather than cleaning them up. No failed services, new network exposure, or package damage was observed.
